meaning: Flow Temperature Overheat Lockout / No Water Flow Lockout - the boiler has locked out because the CH flow temperature exceeded the safe limit, or no water flow was detected through the primary heat exchanger.

causes.cause: System not fully filled/vented or isolation/radiator valves closed
Pump not rotating / pump failure (restricted or no circulation)
Faulty flow or return thermistor giving incorrect reading
Air lock in the system

checks.step: Confirm boiler and CH system filled with water and all isolation/radiator valves open
checks.expected: Pressure gauge reads 1.0-1.5 bar, no closed valves

checks.step: Reset boiler and measure flow/return temperature differential across the boiler
Check pump is rotating freely / check pump operation
checks.expected: Differential falls below 20C once pump runs correctly

checks.step: Check flow and return thermistor resistance (Frame 53 / Section 3.30 pump housing)

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. If caused by low water/no flow, fill and vent the system and open all isolation valves before resetting.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: Ignition Lockout - the boiler failed to detect a flame within the allowed ignition attempts and has locked out.

causes.cause: No or low gas supply pressure to the boiler
Faulty or incorrectly positioned ignition/detection electrode, or poor harness continuity
Blocked condensate pipe/siphon preventing correct operation
Faulty spark generator
Faulty gas valve or gas valve wiring/PCB fault

checks.step: Reset the boiler - does it ignite briefly then extinguish?
Check gas inlet pressure at the boiler
Check detection electrode and harness: continuity, visual condition and position (Frame 55)
checks.expected: Continuity present, electrode clean and correctly positioned

checks.step: Check condensate pipe/siphon for blockage
Check approx. 215 Vdc supply is present at the gas valve
checks.expected: Reading greater than 150V indicates correct supply

checks.step: Check spark generator and associated harness: continuity and visual condition (Frame 56)
Check ignition electrode and harness: continuity, visual condition and position (Frame 54)
Unplug gas valve and check resistance between outside pins
Check wiring continuity from gas valve to PCB

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Check other gas appliances work and that the gas isolation valve under the boiler is open before resetting.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: No Water Flow Lockout - the boiler has locked out because no water flow was detected through the primary heat exchanger.

causes.cause: System not filled/vented or isolation/radiator valves closed
Pump failure or restricted pump rotation
Faulty flow/return thermistor
Faulty no-water-flow thermistor (top of heat exchanger)

checks.step: Confirm boiler and CH system filled with water and all isolation/radiator valves open
Reset boiler and measure flow/return temperature differential
Check pump connection and that pump rotates freely
Check flow and return thermistor resistance (Frame 53)
Check no-water-flow thermistor resistance (Frame 73)

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Fill and vent the system and open all isolation valves before resetting.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: Too Many Resets - the boiler has been reset 5 times within 15 minutes and has locked out to prevent repeated unsuccessful restart attempts.

causes.cause: Repeated, unresolved underlying lockout (e.g. ignition lockout or overheat lockout) triggering the reset counter

checks.step: Check fault history / identify the underlying fault that is causing repeated resets
Turn the electrical power to the boiler off and then on to clear the too-many-resets condition
checks.expected: Boiler re-enters its normal start sequence

reset: Turn the electrical power supply to the boiler off and then on again. Resolve the underlying repeating fault before attempting further resets; contact installer if it persists.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)
source.page: p.56 (Main Menu chart) - Too Many Resets

meaning: False Flame Lockout (referred to in the manual's main fault chart as 'Fault 8') - the boiler has detected a flame signal when no flame should be present.

causes.cause: Deteriorated or faulty flame sense (detection) electrode
Poor continuity / fault in flame detection electrode wiring or in-line connector
Internal boiler wiring routing or integrity fault

checks.step: Reset the boiler - does it work OK afterwards?
Check routing and integrity of internal boiler wiring
Check condition of the flame sense electrode and replace if deteriorated
Separate the flame detection electrode in-line connector and check continuity between the terminal pins connected to the electrode

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: No Water Flow Thermistor Fault - the thermistor located at the top of the heat exchanger used to detect no-water-flow conditions has failed or is incorrectly wired.

causes.cause: Faulty no-water-flow thermistor
Wiring/connector fault between thermistor and PCB low-voltage 11-way connector

checks.step: Disconnect wiring from the no-water-flow thermistor and measure its resistance
Check wiring is securely connected to the low-voltage 11-way connector at the front left of the PCB
Check wiring is securely connected to the no-water-flow thermistor (top of heat exchanger)

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Contact installer - this fault requires an engineer visit.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: Low Water Pressure - the central heating system water pressure has fallen below the minimum required for safe operation.

causes.cause: System water pressure not topped up / undetected leak
Loose or faulty connections on the water pressure sensor
Faulty water pressure sensor

checks.step: Check boiler/CH system is filled with water, pressure gauge reading
Check connections on the water pressure sensor are secure
Top up system pressure via the filling loop

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Fill and vent the system via the filling loop to 1.0-1.5 bar first.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: Flame Loss - the boiler ignited successfully but lost the flame signal during operation.

causes.cause: Interrupted or low gas supply pressure
Faulty/incorrectly positioned ignition/detection electrode
Blocked condensate pipe or blocked flue
Faulty spark generator or gas valve

checks.step: Does the boiler ignite for a short time and then extinguish?
Check gas inlet pressure at the boiler
Check detection electrode and harness: continuity, visual condition and position (Frame 55)
Check condensate pipe and flue for blockage
Check approx. 215 Vdc supply is present at gas valve while flame is on
checks.expected: Reading greater than 150V indicates correct supply

checks.step: Check spark generator and harness: continuity and visual condition (Frame 56)
Check ignition electrode and harness: continuity, visual condition and position (Frame 54)
Check siphon and condensate drain pipework for blockage

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting.

meaning: Fan Fault - the flue fan has failed to operate or run correctly.

causes.cause: Faulty/loose wiring between fan and PCB
Faulty fan motor
Faulty PCB fan drive output

checks.step: Check wiring from fan to PCB: secure connections at both ends, no deterioration, continuity present
Check for 230 Vac at the Blue and Brown connections on the 3-way fan connector

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Contact installer - replace fan or PCB as indicated by the checks.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: Flow Thermistor Fault - the CH flow thermistor has failed or is giving an out-of-range reading.

causes.cause: Faulty flow thermistor
Wiring/connector fault between thermistor and PCB
Faulty PCB

checks.step: Remove flow thermistor from the CH flow pipe and measure resistance across its terminal pins
Check continuity between the PCB and the thermistor wiring

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Fit a new thermistor, repair wiring, or replace PCB as indicated by the checks.

Faulty PCB

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Fit a new thermistor, repair wiring, or replace PCB as indicated by the checks.

meaning: Outside Sensor Fault - the external weather-compensation sensor has failed or is incorrectly wired.

causes.cause: Faulty outside sensor
Wiring fault between outside sensor, terminal block and PCB

checks.step: Disconnect wires to the outside sensor and measure resistance across its terminal pins
Check wiring securely connected between the incoming terminal block connection and the PCB
Check wiring securely connected at both the boiler terminal block and the outside sensor

reset: Official reset procedure: turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately turn the knob back to the required setting. Only required if weather compensation/outside sensor accessory is fitted.

meaning: Low Mains Voltage (shown in the manual's main fault chart as 'Low mains voltage') - the electrical supply voltage to the boiler is outside the acceptable range.

causes.cause: Low or unstable incoming mains electricity supply

checks.step: Measure incoming mains voltage at the boiler terminals L and N

reset: No boiler-side reset is specified; contact the electricity provider to resolve the supply voltage issue, then reset the boiler once supply is restored.

meaning: BCC Activation / PCB Replaced - shown after a new PCB and Boiler Chip Card (BCC) have been fitted, prompting an initial activation reset.

causes.cause: New PCB/BCC just fitted and awaiting the activation reset (expected operational step, not a defect)

checks.step: Confirm the correct BCC for the boiler range/output is fitted, oriented with 'TOP' side up
checks.expected: Correct BCC fitted and correctly oriented

checks.step: Reset the boiler via the mode knob once 'c0' is displayed

reset: Turn the mode knob to the reset position and immediately back to the required setting to activate the new PCB/BCC.

source.manual: Ideal Logic+ Combi 24, 30, 35 - Installation and Servicing (UIN 204978 A04, October 2010)

meaning: Boiler Chip Card (BCC) Fault - the PCB has not recognised a valid Boiler Chip Card for this boiler's range/output.

causes.cause: Incorrect or missing BCC for this specific boiler model/output
BCC not correctly seated or incorrectly oriented in its slot
Faulty PCB

checks.step: Check the correct BCC for the boiler range/output is securely inserted at the front left of the PCB, 'TOP' side up
checks.expected: Correct BCC fitted and correctly oriented

checks.step: Replace with a new, correct BCC, power on until 'c0' is shown, then reset the boiler - is 'c2' still shown?
checks.expected: 'c2' clears after the correct BCC is fitted and the boiler reset

reset: Fit the correct BCC for the boiler, power on until 'c0' is displayed, then turn the mode knob to reset and back. If 'c2' persists with a confirmed correct BCC, replace the PCB.

meaning: The boiler has locked out because the CH flow temperature exceeded the safe limit, or no/insufficient water flow was detected through the primary heat exchanger. Shown as plain text on the LCD status display (this range does not use an alphanumeric fault code).

Restart boiler and measure flow/return temperature differential across the boiler
Check pump is rotating freely
Check flow and return thermistor resistance (Section 3.15 & 3.30)

reset: Press the Restart button on the boiler control panel to restart the boiler. Fill and vent the system and open all isolation valves first if that was the cause.
